text: Lisa Marie Presley (February 1, 1968 – January 12, 2023) was an American singer-songwriter, the daughter of singer and actor Elvis Presley and actress Priscilla Presley, born at Baptist Memorial Hospital-Memphis in Memphis, Tennessee, nine months to the day after her parents' wedding. She was the only child of Elvis and Priscilla Presley and lived with her mother in Los Angeles and frequently stayed with her father at Graceland in Memphis. When she was four, her parents separated, and their divorce was finalized in October 1973. After Elvis died in August 1977, nine-year-old Lisa Marie became a joint heir to his estate with her 61-year-old grandfather Vernon Presley and her 87-year-old great-grandmother Minnie Mae (Hood) Presley; through Vernon, she was a descendant of the Harrison family of Virginia. Following the deaths of her grandfather in 1979 and her great-grandmother in 1980, she became Elvis' sole heir. On her 25th birthday in 1993, she inherited an estate estimated at $100 million and sold 85 percent of Elvis Presley Enterprises in 2004. She released three studio albums—To Whom It May Concern (2003), Now What (2005), and Storm & Grace (2012). To Whom It May Concern was certified gold by the Recording Industry Association of America and reached No. 5 on the Billboard 200, with its first single "Lights Out" reaching No. 18 on the Billboard Hot Adult Top 40 and No. 16 on the UK charts. She wrote all the lyrics (except "The Road Between," which she co-wrote with Gus Black) and co-wrote every melody, and collaborated with Billy Corgan on the B-side track "Savior." Her second album, Now What, reached No. 9 on the Billboard 200, included covers of Don Henley's "Dirty Laundry" (which hit No. 36 on the Billboard 100 AC singles chart) and the Ramones' "Here Today and Gone Tomorrow," and featured a guest appearance by Pink on "Shine." The video for "Dirty Laundry" included a cameo by George Michael. In 2006, she appeared in the music video for Johnny Cash's "God's Gonna Cut You Down," which won the 2008 Grammy Award for Best Short Form Music Video. In 2007, she released "In the Ghetto" as a virtual duet with her father, commemorating the 30th anniversary of his death; the video reached No. 1 on iTunes and No. 16 on the Bubbling Under Hot 100, with proceeds benefiting Presley Place Transitional Housing Campus in New Orleans. She performed the song with the Harlem Gospel Choir on The Oprah Winfrey Show using vintage footage of her father. In 2009, she joined Richard Hawley in London to perform "Weary," and they began a songwriting partnership in which she wrote the lyrics and he composed the music. She planned to release a new album in 2011. Her third album, Storm & Grace, released on May 15, 2012, was produced by T Bone Burnett and described as a stronger, more mature, and more effective work; AllMusic and Spinner.com praised it as a significant achievement, with Entertainment Weekly highlighting the "smoky, spooky" single "You Ain't Seen Nothing Yet." Burnett stated that he heard honesty, rawness, and soulfulness in her music and believed her father would have been proud. In 2018, she was featured on the title track of Where No One Stands Alone, a compilation of her father's gospel recordings, reworked into a duet with him, with a music video digitally incorporating her into scenes with Elvis. Prior to her death, she recorded audio tapes for a memoir, which her daughter Riley Keough completed after her death. The memoir, From Here to the Great Unknown, was published posthumously on October 8, 2024, through Random House, features a photograph of a young Presley with her father on the cover, and is co-authored by Presley and Riley. The Presley Charitable Foundation (PCF), formed in 2007 and reincorporated as The Presley Foundation Inc. on November 10, 2022, registered as a public benefit and grantmaking foundation on February 13, 2023; it funds Presley Place, which provides homeless families with rent-free housing, child day care, career and financial counseling, and family-management guidance, and the Elvis Presley Music Room, where children have access to instruments and instruction. The EPCF also established the Elvis Presley Endowed Scholarship Fund at the University of Memphis for students in the arts. Presley volunteered in relief efforts after Hurricane Katrina, distributing supplies in Mississippi and helping at food banks and stores in Memphis, stating, "I'm here because I definitely needed to do something," and filling a truck with groceries and toiletries. In 2011, she became a patron of the Dream Factory in Hainault, London. She participated in the Grammy Foundation's Gold Grammy Signature Schools program and presented a special award to Isaac Hayes at the Memphis Recording Academy Honors on October 22, 2005, alongside Justin Timberlake, David Porter, and music producer Jimmy Jam. On November 11, 2005, she participated in a Grammy SoundCheck at LA's House of Blues with music students. In 2005, she appeared in the television film Elvis by the Presleys. Between 2010 and 2016, she lived in a 15th-century manor house in Rotherfield, East Sussex, England, 15 miles east of Saint Hill Manor, the British headquarters of the Church of Scientology. She publicly acknowledged her struggle with opioid addiction, writing the foreword to United States of Opioids: A Prescription for Liberating a Nation in Pain (2019), stating she had been prescribed opioids after the birth of her twin daughters in 2008 and became dependent on them, and had been using them again in the weeks prior to her death on January 12, 2023. On October 3, 1988, she married Danny Keough at the Scientology Celebrity Centre in Los Angeles, after dating for three years; their honeymoon took place on a cruise ship owned by the Church of Scientology. After an early abortion she later described as "the stupidest thing she has ever done," they had two children: Riley Keough (born May 29, 1989), and Benjamin Storm Keough (born October 21, 1992), delivered via a "Silent birth" according to Church of Scientology practice. She obtained a quickie divorce in the Dominican Republic on May 6, 1994. Later that year, Keough considered seeking custody of their children due to child-molestation charges against Michael Jackson, whom she married after her divorce. In a 2003 interview, she addressed reports of a planned remarriage to Keough, stating, "Danny is my best friend, always has been, always will be. I love him unconditionally, but we are not together. It's not like that." After her divorce from Jackson, she and Keough grew closer; in 2005, Keough played bass in her band and served as her musical mentor, and she continued to regard him as a close friend, saying they had a special, unconditional bond and were like brother and sister. She told People in 2005, "You don't have to put your crap on your kids even if you are not together. You can still be civilized." They remained close friends until her death in 2023. Her daughter Riley married Ben Smith-Petersen in 2015, and their daughter, Presley's grandchild, was born in 2022; in 2025, Priscilla confirmed Riley and Smith-Petersen welcomed a second child. Benjamin died on July 12, 2020, at age 27 in Calabasas, California, from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, classified as suicide; Presley was devastated and struggled profoundly in the years that followed. On May 26, 1994, twenty days after her divorce from Keough, she married Michael Jackson. Keough's younger brother served as an official witness at the wedding. Presley and Jackson first met in 1974 when a six-year-old Presley attended one of his concerts at the Sahara Tahoe; according to a friend, their adult friendship began in November 1992 in L.A. In a 2010 interview with Oprah Winfrey, she stated she believed Jackson did not do anything wrong and was wrongly accused, and that she had fallen for him, wanting to save him, and persuaded him to settle the allegations out of court and enter rehabilitation. She appeared in Jackson's "You Are Not Alone" music video in June 1995. In January 1996, citing irreconcilable differences, she filed for divorce. Jackson's make-up artist, Karen Faye, claimed he initially planned to file first but relented after Presley asked him not to; the next day, she filed herself. In the same 2010 interview, she said they attempted to reconcile intermittently for four years after their divorce and that she had traveled internationally to be with him. After Jackson's death in 2009 at age 50, she was reported to have "felt shattered."

Lisa Marie Presley began developing a deep emotional connection with Michael Jackson, stating, "I started falling for him. I wanted to save him. I felt that I could do it," and shortly after, persuaded Jackson to settle allegations out of court and enter rehabilitation. Presley appeared in Jackson's "You Are Not Alone" music video in June 1995, directed by Wayne Isham. In January 1996, citing irreconcilable differences, Presley filed for divorce; Jackson's make-up artist Karen Faye claimed he had initially planned to file first but relented after Presley asked him not to, only to learn the next day that she had filed herself. In a 2010 interview with Oprah Winfrey, Presley said they attempted to reconcile intermittently for four years after their divorce, traveling internationally to be with Jackson, and described her emotional bond as intense, stating, "I felt like I just always wanted to be around him, always wanted to be part of – I felt so high. I’ve never felt like that around another human being..." She also said she was the last person standing over Jackson's casket after his death in 2009 at age 50, adding, "I didn’t want to leave him." In a 2014 interview with The Sydney Morning Herald, Presley noted that too much had occurred between them due to external interference, saying, "With MJ [Michael Jackson], unfortunately, too much happened, too much got between us. There was a very deep strong love there; intense. But people got in the way, on my end and his end. We had so many people telling us what to do and intercepting and speaking on behalf of the other. Had it been just he and I, towards the end, I don't think we would have divorced." In her 2024 memoir, From Here to the Great Unknown, she wrote, "I've never been that happy again," referring to her time with Jackson. In May 1999, Presley met musician John Oszajca and became engaged two days before Christmas, ending the engagement in March 2001 after meeting Nicolas Cage at a party. Presley married Cage in Kamuela, Hawaii, on August 10, 2002, and he filed for divorce 107 days later on November 25, 2002, with the divorce finalized on May 24, 2004. On January 22, 2006, in Kyoto, Japan, Presley married for the fourth time to Michael Lockwood, her guitarist, music producer, and musical director, with Keough serving as best man. In March 2008, Presley announced she was pregnant, and Lockwood became a first-time father. On October 7, 2008, she gave birth via Caesarean section to fraternal twin daughters, Harper Vivienne Ann Lockwood and Finley Aaron Love Lockwood, at Los Robles Hospital & Medical Center in Thousand Oaks, California. The couple maintained a home in England at Coes Manor in Rotherfield, East Sussex. In 2016, Presley filed for divorce from Lockwood after ten years of marriage. In February 2017, the couple's children were placed in temporary care with Priscilla after Lisa Marie alleged in a court filing that she had discovered inappropriate images of children on Lockwood's personal computer while contesting his request for spousal support. The Beverly Hills Police Department investigated, examining over 80 electronic devices, and found no criminal activity, referring the matter to Tennessee authorities, which later closed the inquiry in 2017 citing no evidence of a crime. The divorce was finalized on May 26, 2021. Presley, along with friend and fellow Memphian and Scientologist Isaac Hayes, opened the Literacy, Education and Ability Program (LEAP) in October 1997, operated by Applied Scholastics, an organization run by Scientologists. For her efforts to help U.S. children develop study skills, she received the Humanitarian Award from the Church of Scientology-supported World Literacy Crusade on January 5, 2002, from Hayes, Chaka Khan, and Yolanda King, daughter of Martin Luther King Jr. Critics regard the World Literacy Crusade as a front group for the Church of Scientology. On September 26, 2002, Presley addressed a U.S. congressional hearing in opposition to medication use in treating ADHD, stating, "I have spoken to children who have been forced to take a cocaine-like stimulant to control their behavior. I have shared their sense of sheer desperation. Children have been wrenched from their family's care simply because their parents favored an alternative, drug-free approach to addressing educational and behavioral problems. The psychotropic drugging of millions of children has to stop," addressing the committee as the International Spokesperson for Children's Rights for the Citizens Commission on Human Rights (CCHR), an organization run by Scientologists, and arguing parents should be informed about alternatives to medication. Presley left Scientology in 2014, though she had been experiencing growing discontent as early as 2008. On January 12, 2023, at approximately 10:30 a.m., Presley suffered cardiac arrest at her home in Calabasas, California. Emergency responders administered CPR, and she regained a pulse before being transported to West Hills Hospital in Los Angeles, where she died later that day at age 54. According to the autopsy report, she died from a small bowel obstruction caused by complications of a prior bariatric surgery; a toxicology analysis found opioids in her system, but they were not considered a factor in her death. Her last public appearance was two days earlier at the 80th Golden Globe Awards, which she attended with her mother. Hundreds attended her public memorial service at Graceland on January 22, and more than 1.5 million people watched it via live stream. Presley was interred in the Graceland Meditation Garden, next to her son Benjamin and adjacent to her father, Elvis. Attendees included her mother; her surviving children; family friend Jerry Schilling; former Memphis mayor A. C. Wharton; Guns N' Roses lead singer Axl Rose; The Smashing Pumpkins lead singer Billy Corgan; Sarah, Duchess of York; gospel quartet The Blackwood Brothers; singer Alanis Morissette; and the director and star of Elvis, Baz Luhrmann and Austin Butler. On the CBS primetime special The Presleys: Elvis, Lisa Marie and Riley, which aired on October 8, 2024, Presley's daughter Riley told Oprah Winfrey that Presley's final years were marked by profound grief, with the loss of her son Benjamin leaving her without the will to keep living. After Elvis's death on August 16, 1977, his will appointed his father Vernon as executor and trustee, with beneficiaries Vernon, Elvis's grandmother Minnie Mae, and Lisa Marie, whose inheritance was to be held in trust until her 25th birthday. After Vernon's death in 1979, Priscilla was named one of three trustees, along with the National Bank of Commerce in Memphis and Joseph Hanks, the Presleys' accountant. With Minnie Mae's death in 1980, Lisa Marie became the sole surviving beneficiary. In 1993, Presley inherited her father's estate on her 25th birthday, which—thanks largely to her mother's stewardship—had grown to an estimated $100 million. In 1998, Presley became more closely involved in managing the Elvis Presley Trust and its business entity, Elvis Presley Enterprises, Inc., serving as owner and chairman of the board until February 2005, when she sold 85 percent of the estate's business holdings to CKX, Inc., excluding Graceland itself and the property within it. Following Presley's death, her three daughters were expected to inherit Graceland, but her mother Priscilla challenged a 2016 amendment Presley made to her estate, which removed Priscilla as trustee and named her two oldest children. One of them, Presley's son Benjamin, died by suicide in 2020, leaving Riley as sole trustee. On August 16, 2024, Missouri woman Lisa Jeanine Findley was arrested for a scheme involving a fraudulent claim that Presley owed money to illegally force the sale of Graceland. According to the U.S. Department of Justice's Office of Public Affairs, Findley "allegedly fabricated loan documents" on which she "forged the signatures of Elvis Presley’s daughter and a Florida State notary public. Findley then allegedly filed a false creditor’s claim with the Superior Court of California in Los Angeles, and a fake deed of trust with the Shelby County Register’s Office in Memphis" and "allegedly published a fraudulent foreclosure notice." One person involved in the scheme told The New York Times in May 2024 that the plot was connected to a ring of identity thieves based in Nigeria who claimed Presley owed $2.8 million to Naussany Investments & Private Lending LLC, which was not a real company, and the identity thieves routinely used forgeries of recently deceased individuals to carry out fraud schemes. As a central figure in facilitating the attempted sale of Graceland, Findley "posed as three different individuals" associated with the "fictitious private lender" to falsely claim that Presley had borrowed $3.8 million from Naussany Investments in 2018. The loan documents purportedly signed by Presley had allegedly been acknowledged before Kimberly L. Philbrick, a Florida notary public, who in an affidavit stated, "I have never met Lisa Marie Presley, nor have I ever notarized a document signed by Lisa Marie Presley. ... I do not know why my signature appears on this document." In February 2012, Presley opened a new exhibit, "Elvis ... Through His Daughter's Eyes," included in the Graceland VIP Tour and featuring 200 items assembled by Presley and the Graceland Archives staff, exploring her experience of growing up with a famous father, with home movies, toys, and rarely seen family mementos on display. In November 1975, her father named one of his private aircraft, a converted Convair 880 jet, after her. He spent more than $1 million refurbishing it for use as his main transport while on tour. The Lisa Marie and one of his other planes, Hound Dog II, are on exhibit at Graceland. On June 24, 2011, Presley was officially honored by the governor of Tennessee, Bill Haslam, who proclaimed a day of recognition for her charitable efforts. Two days later, she received a Certificate of Proclamation from the mayor of New Orleans, Mitchell J. Landrieu, in recognition of her dedication and contributions to the city. She was also issued a proclamation by the city of Memphis on June 28, 2011, for her philanthropy there.
